newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil- Prices softer in thin market.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil- Prices softer in thin market.

text.p: The high sulphur fuel oil market was softer in thin talks on Friday despite slight gains in crude values and swaps, traders said.
Kuwait sold an 80,000-tonne cargo to a major at a premium of $1.10 per tonne over Singapore's publishd quotes on a cost-and-freight (c-and-f) basis for April delivery to Singapore, traders said.
The 180-cst grade was heard offered at $101 per tonne for delivery between late March and early April, with a bid from a local trading company at $98, traders said.
Demand from China remained poor, although some traders believed several scheduled maintenance turnarounds in Singapore later this month could digest some supplies and support prices.
Fuel oil sawps inched slightly higher, with March at $98.25/$99.75 and April at $95.50/$96.50 compared with Thursday's $98.00/$99.00 and $95.50/96.25 respectively.
Enquiries from China for April cargoes continued, but most Chinese buyers were still largely sidelined.
Poor demand in the LSWR market continued to weaken prices, traders said.
(Prices in dollars per tonne, unless stated)
